businessType: Industrial equipment manufacturer (pumps, valves, controls) serving oil/gas, water, chemical industries. $180M revenue, 650 employees, 3 manufacturing facilities (US + Mexico), distributed through 200+ distributors + 12% direct. Established in 1988, family-owned, now managed by second generation with professional ops team.
stage: Mature profitable: EBITDA $28M (15.6% margin, down from 18% 24mo ago), gross margin 42% (down from 46%), operating cash flow $18M. Supply chain disruptions (post-COVID, semiconductor shortages, logistics) driving cost increases.
ownerGoal: Restore EBITDA margin to 18%+ within 18 months to position for potential PE acquisition.
ownerConstraints: Supply chain risk: Semiconductor components sourced globally; shortages driving 15-20% cost increases on electronic controls. Substitute suppliers limited and qual takes 6-12 months.

Pricing power limited: Highly competitive market; price increases met with customer push-back. OEM customers (who buy direct) have long contracts (2-3 year lock, price-adjust clauses capped at 5% annually). Distributors will shift sourcing if prices rise too much.
Margin structure: Gross margin 42% supports overhead (engineering, sales, ops), leaving limited EBITDA even with cost discipline. Volume leverage is critical.

Manufacturing footprint: Mexico plant underutilized due to logistics costs (tariffs, freight); US plants operating at 85% utilization. Consolidation would improve leverage but require capex and disruption.
Working capital: Extended customer payment terms (60-90 days standard in industry) tie up significant cash. Inventory buildup due to supply uncertainty consuming cash.
immediateConcern: EBITDA margin eroding rapidly: down 240bps in 24 months (18% → 15.6%). Cost of goods sold rising faster than revenue (supply chain pressures) while selling price relatively flat. Operating leverage working in reverse. At current trajectory, EBITDA margin could drop to 14% within 12 months, making PE acquisition unviable. Must address whether problem is structural (market/supply chain headwinds), operational (manufacturing inefficiency or overhead bloat), or strategic (product mix shift to lower-margin products).

Manufacturing efficiency: Where is utilization opportunity? What is the cost of Mexico under-utilization? Consolidation impact?

riskAppetite: MEDIUM (mature company with stable cash flow; PE owner wants growth but valuation multiples matter)
